speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what are the estimated benefits of the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) for the first three years when it is implemented; (b) which industries will benefit most from CPTPP; and (c) how will the Ministry educate and promote the benefits of CPTPP to the local companies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Many industries and sectors will be able to benefit from CPTPP.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: First, Singapore-based goods producers will benefit from preferential tariffs when exporting to a CPTPP market.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Second, service providers will benefit from preferential access in a wide range of sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Examples include transport and distribution services in Australia, energy and telecommunications in Mexico, and professional services in Canada.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Beyond specific business opportunities, the value of CPTPP is in establishing a common set of enforceable rules that govern trade and investment in the 21st century.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These include rules in the areas of e-commerce, innovative industries and provisions to help small and medium-sized enterprises.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) is working with our agencies, and the Singapore Business Federation (SBF) and other trade associations and chambers to conduct outreach sessions to our companies on how to benefit from CPTPP.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our economic agencies, including Enterprise Singapore (ESG) and the Economic Development Board (EDB), are also at hand to facilitate companies' plans to access or establish supply chains in the CPTPP markets.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: What is the timeframe for the rest of the countries to ratify CPTPP and whether the United States (US) has indicated an interest to join CPTPP?
